results.correct_value: Non-glaciated single-day scramble from the Twin Lakes trailhead via the High Pass Trail, the col in Larrabee's south arm, the basin and the gully to the Peak 1-2 notch; no Ptarmigan Ridge, Camp Kiser or glacier travel.
results.evidence: SummitPost's Pleiades page describes the approach from Twin Lakes Road 3065 via the High Pass trail, then scree/snow to the col in Larrabee's south arm, the basin and the gully to the notch between the 1st and 2nd Pleiades. A 2025 trip report drove to the Twin Lakes trailhead, went over High Pass and climbed all four peaks in a single day with no glacier. The Forest Service High Pass Trail page places the route out of Twin Lakes. Ptarmigan Ridge/Camp Kiser is on Mount Baker, unrelated.

results.evidence: The Forest Service High Pass Trail page warns that steep, exposed snowfields linger into August and an ice axe is needed before they melt, so early July is not optimal. A 2025 trip report climbed all four peaks on September 19 in good conditions, and a High Pass hike report is dated September 30. The glacier-based reasons for calling September risky do not apply; there is no glacier.

results.evidence: The Forest Service Twin Lakes Trailhead, High Pass Trail 676 and Winchester Mountain Trail 685 pages list only a recreation pass (NW Forest Pass/Interagency or day fee) plus Mount Baker Wilderness rules (party of 12, no campfires) and say nothing of a required wilderness permit; WTA lists only the pass. The Forest Service permits page names a required self-issue permit only for Alpine Lakes Wilderness. No source was found that states either that a Mount Baker Wilderness self-issue permit is required at Twin Lakes or explicitly that none is; absence from the pages is not two affirmative sources.
